answer: Reputation Decay Curve: each identity’s influence grows as a falcon curve—slow at first, steep only after sustained activity—so fresh accounts carry near-zero weight. To reach useful influence, an attacker must run each identity through that full delay, paying the compute, time, and coordination cost separately per sybil. A jetty of parallel identities does not help, since weight cannot be pooled across them. Monthly inactivity decay forces continuous spend to hold rank. The lotus effect: only aged, active identities bloom, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
